critical_code_review_comments: Login.js L353-389 — validateStatus whitelist (200-299 OR 401/403/404/409/429) correctly lets 202 reach the success path. Manual re-throw for status>=400 keeps 401/403/4xx errors going through the existing toast/error handling. context_for_next_testing_agent: iter66 is GREEN. The pending-approval flow is now properly wired end-to-end FROM the user's perspective: B's login UI shows the awaiting-approval banner the instant the backend returns 202. Production note: existing user_sessions in the live DB that pre-date iter66 will have NO last_seen_at field, and will therefore be treated as 'stale' by the active_other gating until the user's device next pings /auth/me. This is fine (and is what unblocked the user-reported false-positive 'phantom approval prompt from a closed-tab device') but if iter67 wants to be extra-safe, run a one-time backfill: db.user_sessions.updateMany({last_seen_at: {$exists: false}}, {$set: {last_seen_at: new Date().toISOString()}}). The iter62::test_full_flow_register_verify_login 500 (pymongo update_one in verify_email) is the only outstanding item — needs a look but not blocking. Backend size keeps growing (7561 lines), would benefit from a split refactor in a dedicated cleanup iter.
rca of the issue: User-reported bug: 'no waiting message on B during 2nd-device login'. RCA confirmed by iter66: axios default validateStatus treats 2xx as success and only 4xx/5xx as throw. The old Login.js code put the 202 handler INSIDE a catch(err2) block — but axios never threw for 202, so the catch never ran → setPendingApproval(...) was never called → banner never showed → user thought login was silently broken. FIX: added validateStatus to allow 202 (and the manually-handled 401/403/404/409/429) through axios's success path, then branched on res.status===202 explicitly. Validated live on real mobile viewport with real backend roundtrip. Secondary improvement: last_seen_at heartbeat — a session whose owner has closed the tab >10min ago is no longer treated as 'active', so it no longer triggers a useless approval modal on a device nobody is watching. Both fixes are minimal, surgical, and backward-compatible.
